title: Reject extra mounts containing original checkouts or sensitive host paths
description: Review finding: validate_extra_mount in src/paths.rs rejects a source within the original repository, but not a source that is an ancestor of it. The sensitive() check rejects a handful of exact paths and descendants, but permits ancestors such as the user home directory. A configured extra mount of the home directory therefore passes validation while exposing the original checkout and credential directories to the Kata guest. Resolve/canonicalize the source as today, then reject paths that contain any original checkout or protected credential/state path, including parent directories. Add tests for ancestor mounts (home, parent of repo, parent of runtime socket/credential store) and symlink aliases. Revisit any legitimate narrow allowlisted mounts before blocking broad paths.
acceptance_criteria: Host mount validation rejects ancestors of original checkouts, credential directories, and runtime sockets while preserving safe disjoint mounts; focused unit tests cover parent mounts and symlink aliases.

title: Fix jbox prime loading vhost_net
description: Problem: jbox prime passes vhost_vsock and vhost_net to one modprobe invocation. Modprobe treats vhost_net as a parameter to vhost_vsock, confirmed by the kernel log, so the vhost_net module remains unloaded and Internet-enabled guest sessions cannot start. Reproduction: run jbox prime while vhost_net is unloaded, then observe the readiness check fail and journalctl report the ignored parameter. Change: invoke modprobe separately for each module, preserve root and sudo behavior, and add focused tests. Acceptance: prime independently loads both modules, tests cover root and sudo command construction, and the Rust quality gates pass.
acceptance_criteria: Prime invokes separate modprobe calls for vhost_vsock and vhost_net. Unit tests cover root and sudo forms. Full Rust quality gate passes.
notes: Diagnosis from the affected Manjaro host: vhost_net exists for kernel 6.18.49-1-MANJARO and vhost_vsock loaded, but vhost_net remained absent. The kernel journal recorded vhost_vsock: unknown parameter vhost_net ignored, proving that the original combined modprobe invocation passed the second module as a parameter. Implementation now runs a separate modprobe command for each module. Static validation passed: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --all-targets, cargo run -- --help, and git diff --check. Manual host verification using the newly built binary remains pending because sudo requires the interactive user terminal.

title: Implement history-preserving Beads bootstrap guard
description: Apply the selected repository-level guard so routine agent and contributor startup cannot create an embedded Beads database that omits the tracked issue export. Preserve no-git-ops intent and avoid destructive initialization.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh clone follows the normal documented startup path and retains all tracked issues before its first write. Existing healthy databases are not overwritten. The change preserves no-git-ops behavior.
close_reason: Added first-run bootstrap instructions to AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md. A fresh isolated clone successfully ran bd bootstrap --yes, bd prime, and bd ready with all tracked issues present and no working-tree changes.

title: Characterize no-git Beads initialization and choose a safe guard
description: Reproduce the export divergence in an isolated clone, inspect the bootstrap and hook behavior, and identify a deterministic non-destructive initialization path that preserves tracked JSONL history. Record the exact command sequence and proposed repository-level guard.
acceptance_criteria: An isolated reproduction identifies the triggering command sequence and whether bootstrap, hooks, or project configuration can prevent it. The selected guard is non-destructive and has documented rationale.
notes: Findings: In a fresh clone, bd bootstrap --dry-run selects import from the tracked .beads/issues.jsonl. Running bd status before bootstrap fails with no database and does not create one. Running bd bootstrap --yes imports all 10 tracked issues, and a subsequent scratch issue creation retained every original exported ID. With no-git-ops, the scratch write did not alter the tracked JSONL. Project hook source scripts deliberately skip when no database exists, and cloned repositories do not have installed Git hooks. Selected guard: require bd bootstrap --yes before bd prime or any regular bd command in contributor and agent instructions. This is non-destructive for fresh clones because bootstrap imports tracked history, and it only validates an existing database. Stale existing databases require the explicit recovery workflow planned in jbox-bwu.
close_reason: Isolated fresh-clone tests confirmed non-destructive bootstrap behavior and selected documented bootstrap guard.

title: Prevent no-git Beads state from replacing tracked issue export
description:
## Problem
During the 2026-09-23 repository review, the first Beads create after the no-git-ops configuration was enabled changed .beads/issues.jsonl from five historical closed issues to only the new review issue plus a reopened jbox-ods. The embedded database was missing tracked issue history until a supported import recovered it. Diagnose the migration, bootstrap, and export behavior and ensure creating or updating issues cannot silently drop or reopen tracked history.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Use a repository with tracked .beads/issues.jsonl history and no-git-ops enabled.
2. Ensure the embedded database lacks the tracked history.
3. Create an issue with bd and inspect the JSONL export.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh clone with no-git-ops enabled retains or imports existing tracked issue history before writes. Beads writes do not silently drop or reopen historical issues in .beads/issues.jsonl. Regression coverage or documented deterministic recovery is provided.
close_reason: Completed non-destructive Beads startup guard and recovery guidance. Fresh-clone bootstrap and tracked-history preservation were verified in isolated clones.

title: Make GitHub CLI skill-mount test hermetic for CI
description: The first Rust Quality GitHub Actions run failed because tests::skills_repository_mount_includes_writable_gh_metadata_parent reads the runner host GitHub CLI credential file at src/lib.rs:4442. The test passes locally only when a host gh login exists. Refactor the test to provide an isolated credential fixture so cargo test --all-targets is independent of host authentication.
acceptance_criteria: The affected test creates and uses its own safe GitHub CLI hosts fixture or equivalent isolated path. cargo test --all-targets passes without any host gh login. The Rust Quality workflow passes on GitHub Actions.
close_reason: Changed the public-skill mount test to use credentials none and assert that no host GitHub CLI hosts file is mounted. Verified it with an empty XDG config path and by running the full Rust suite.

title: Verify Beads recovery flow and document onboarding
description: Add a repeatable verification of the protected fresh-clone path and document a deterministic recovery procedure for an already stale embedded database. Ensure the documented procedure never deletes issue history.
acceptance_criteria: Verification covers fresh setup and stale-state recovery. Contributor instructions specify the safe startup command and recovery steps. Beads lint passes.
notes: Verification evidence: an isolated fresh clone ran bd bootstrap --yes, bd prime, and bd ready successfully. Bootstrap imported every tracked issue and left the Git working tree clean. The current recovery command bd import --dry-run identifies the tracked JSONL as its source. During the original review, importing that tracked JSONL into the stale embedded database restored the previously omitted historical issues without deleting the newly created review issue. AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md now document both first-run bootstrap and non-destructive stale-state recovery, including the prohibition on bd init --force.
close_reason: Documented and verified fresh-clone bootstrap plus non-destructive stale-database recovery.

title: Restore clean Rust formatting and zero-warning Clippy
description:
## Problem
Review on 2026-09-23 found that the formatting check fails across src/config.rs, src/git.rs, and src/lib.rs with rustfmt 1.9.0. Static analysis with Clippy configured to deny warnings also fails on collapsible_if at src/lib.rs lines 1517 through 1522. Format the source and address the lint, then make both commands pass.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run the repository formatting check.
2. Run Clippy for all targets with warnings denied.
acceptance_criteria: The formatting check succeeds. Clippy with warnings denied succeeds. All tests continue to pass.
close_reason: Applied rustfmt across the source tree and collapsed the nested preview patch condition in src/lib.rs. Verified cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --all-targets, CLI help, and git diff --check.

title: Streamline host-side testing of Jbox changes
description: Provide a reversible workflow to test and optionally retain changes from an isolated Jbox session without manually managing host overlays, patches, or duplicate commits.
notes: Design: introduce flag-free `jbox preview` as the canonical host-native review workflow. It freezes the guest, creates an isolated preview worktree from the session dirty state, and opens a local shell. A subsequent `jbox preview` discards and recreates the preview after confirmation. `jbox accept` detects an active preview, adopts its exact state into the session branch, checkpoints it, and accepts into the current host branch. `jbox resume` and `jbox clean` must reject active previews.
close_reason: Implemented and validated the flag-free preview-to-accept workflow.
